data.etymology: Lacrima belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Tear Drop.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lacrima total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
data.cultural_impact: The name Lacrima might evoke images of the Catholic tradition of the tears of Mary, specifically in relation to the sorrowing Mother of God. In art, literature, and religious practices, the tears of Mary symbolize her compassion, love, and empathy towards humanity, especially in moments of suffering and trials (Caldwell, 2010). This name could also be related to Jesus' tears at the grave of Lazarus (John 11:35) or His suffering and agony in the Garden of Gethsemane (Matthew 26:38).
data.spiritual_significance: Lacrima carries a profound spiritual significance as it reminds us of the deep emotional depth of our human experiences. It is a reminder that even in times of profound sorrow and painful trials, there is a divine presence and comfort found in the tears we shed. The name Lacrima echoes the words of scripture, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted (Matthew 5:4)," and calls us to embrace the mystery of human emotion, drawing us closer to God in our moments of deepest need.
